overall: Saturday will be a warm but cloudy and stormy day in Washington, DC, with widespread showers and thunderstorms likely through much of the daytime — especially the morning hours — before precipitation chances gradually ease late afternoon. An active Flash Flood Warning expires in the early overnight hours, and an 80% precipitation probability combined with persistent cloud cover will significantly suppress daytime heating relative to today's observed high of 91.4°F. East winds near 7 mph and deep cloud cover will limit how much temperatures can rise.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show moderate spread: HRRR is the warm outlier at ~86.6°F and GFS is the cool outlier at ~78.5°F, while NBM (~83.6°F), ECMWF (~82.0°F), and WEATHER_COM (~81.1°F) cluster in the low-to-mid 80s. The full ensemble blends to an expected TMAX of 83.5°F, closely consistent with the NWS narrative of 'near 84°F,' suggesting reasonable inter-model agreement despite GFS and HRRR anchoring the tails.
max_temp_prediction: The best estimate for tomorrow's high is approximately 83.5°F, with the even-bucket ensemble placing 41.7% probability on 84-85°F and 31.1% on 82-83°F. For the active Kalshi odd-bucket market, the top bucket of 83-84°F (25.2%) aligns squarely with the ensemble mean and NWS forecast, making it the highest-confidence single target, though the adjacent 81-82°F bucket (24.8%) is nearly equally likely — the GFS-driven cooler scenario (78-81°F range) deserves some caution weighting given the heavy precipitation and cloud cover forecast.
